mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: A transverse wave traveling along a string is described by y(x,t) = 0.05 sin[2π(5t - 2x)], where y is in metres, x in metres and t in seconds. What are the wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period of this wave?
mcqs.explanation: The wave equation can be written as y = A sin[2π(ft - x/λ)]. Comparing with the given argument 2π(5t - 2x) gives f = 5 Hz and 1/λ = 2 m⁻¹, so λ = 0.5 m. The amplitude A is the coefficient outside the sine, 0.05 m. The period T is the reciprocal of frequency, T = 1/f = 0.2 s. Option A lists all these correctly; the other options contain at least one wrong value.

mcqs.question: In a stadium, spectators perform the "wave" by standing up and sitting down sequentially around the arena. Which statement best defines the wave motion observed in this scenario?

options.A: A disturbance that propagates through a medium with transfer of energy but no net transport of matter.
options.B: A periodic motion of individual spectators about a fixed position.
options.C: A transfer of matter from one part of the stadium to another.
options.D: A random motion of spectators without any organized pattern.

mcqs.answer: A disturbance that propagates through a medium with transfer of energy but no net transport of matter.
mcqs.explanation: The stadium crowd acts as the medium. The standing‑sitting action is a disturbance that moves around the arena, carrying energy (the excitement) while each person returns to the original seat, so there is no net movement of matter. This matches the definition of wave motion. Options B, C and D describe individual or incorrect aspects and do not capture the essence of a wave.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about mechanical and electromagnetic waves?

options.A: Mechanical waves can travel through vacuum, while electromagnetic waves require a material medium.
options.B: Electromagnetic waves do not need a material medium to propagate.
options.C: Mechanical waves involve oscillations of particles in the medium.
options.D: Electromagnetic waves can travel at the speed of light in vacuum.

mcqs.answer: Mechanical waves can travel through vacuum, while electromagnetic waves require a material medium.
mcqs.explanation: Mechanical waves (e.g., sound, seismic) need a material medium; they cannot travel in vacuum. Electromagnetic waves (e.g., light, radio) do not need a medium. Therefore statement A is the misconception. Statements B, C, and D are correct facts.

mcqs.question: In a transverse wave traveling along a stretched string, the direction of the particle displacement is:

options.A: Parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
options.B: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
options.C: Opposite to the direction of wave propagation.

mcqs.answer: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, in a transverse wave the particles of the medium move at right angles (perpendicular) to the direction in which the wave travels. Option B states this correctly. Options A and C describe longitudinal motion, and D is not characteristic of any organized wave.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly compares transverse and longitudinal waves?

options.A: In transverse waves, particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation; in longitudinal waves, it is perpendicular.
options.B: Both transverse and longitudinal waves require a medium to propagate.
options.C: Transverse waves have particle displacement perpendicular to propagation, while longitudinal waves have displacement parallel to propagation.
options.D: Longitudinal waves can only occur in solids, whereas transverse waves occur only in liquids.

mcqs.answer: Transverse waves have particle displacement perpendicular to propagation, while longitudinal waves have displacement parallel to propagation.
mcqs.explanation: The key distinction is the orientation of particle motion: transverse – perpendicular; longitudinal – parallel. Option C states this accurately. Option A reverses the definitions. Option B is false because electromagnetic transverse waves travel without a material medium. Option D is incorrect; both types can occur in various media (e.g., sound is longitudinal in gases, water surface waves are transverse).

mcqs.learning_point: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period
mcqs.question: A sound wave in air has a frequency of 440 Hz and travels with a speed of 340 m s⁻¹. Which set of values correctly gives its wavelength, period, and a possible amplitude of 0.02 m?
mcqs.explanation: Wavelength λ = v/f = 340 / 440 ≈ 0.7727 m ≈ 0.77 m. Period T = 1/f = 1/440 s ≈ 0.00227 s = 2.27 ms. The amplitude can be any positive value; 0.02 m is a plausible choice. Option A matches all three quantities. Option B uses an incorrect wavelength, C gives an incorrect period, and D changes the amplitude.

mcqs.question: Which statement best defines wave motion?

options.A: A periodic disturbance that travels through a medium, transferring energy without permanent displacement of particles.
options.B: A motion where particles permanently move from one location to another.
options.C: A random vibration of particles in a medium.
options.D: A static deformation of a medium.

mcqs.answer: A periodic disturbance that travels through a medium, transferring energy without permanent displacement of particles.
mcqs.explanation: Wave motion is characterized by a repeating disturbance that moves through a medium (or vacuum for EM waves) and carries energy, while the individual particles of the medium oscillate about their equilibrium positions and return, i.e., no net transport. Option A captures this definition. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated phenomena.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly identifies a mechanical wave and an electromagnetic wave?

options.A: Sound wave in air (mechanical) and light wave in vacuum (electromagnetic).
options.B: Light wave in vacuum (mechanical) and sound wave in air (electromagnetic).
options.C: Radio wave in vacuum (mechanical) and seismic wave in earth (electromagnetic).
options.D: Water wave in ocean (electromagnetic) and X‑ray in space (mechanical).

mcqs.answer: Sound wave in air (mechanical) and light wave in vacuum (electromagnetic).
mcqs.explanation: Sound requires a material medium (air) and is a mechanical wave. Light propagates through vacuum without a medium and is an electromagnetic wave. Option A correctly pairs them. The other options incorrectly label the nature of the waves.
